criterion_notes.c1: Examines household and community access to domestic water supply (and links to basic sanitation) in South Africa under the 2001 Free Basic Water policy.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies both the plain wording of Criterion 2 and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism clarification: under the plain wording, it examines national water legislation, constitutional rights, decentralization, and municipal governance; under the narrow rule-type reading, it directly examines tariff and cost-recovery rules (Section 9 Water Services Act rising block tariff regulations and the 6,000 litres per household per month zero-tariff block), municipal indigent eligibility screening, and rationing via communal standpipe service levels governing household water access.
criterion_notes.c3: Does not contain original empirical evidence or a systematic empirical synthesis. Written by the former Director-General of the Department of Water Affairs and Forestry (1997-2005), this is a narrative policy overview and historical reflection essay that recounts policy formulation, quotes legislation, court affidavits, and civil society debates, and cites descriptive secondary statistics from government reports without any primary data collection, empirical study design, or systematic review methodology (exclude under E05).
criterion_notes.c4: Discusses outcomes relevant to water access, affordability, consumption restraint, and errors of inclusion and exclusion, citing secondary summary figures from DWAF and published reports (e.g., percentage of the total and poor population served by free basic water across municipalities).
criterion_notes.c5: While the national policy context, tariff/subsidy exposure, and broad access concepts are described, there is no empirical study population/sample, analytical unit of observation, or identifiable empirical study design because the article is a non-empirical policy overview.
criterion_notes.c6: Published in English, an eligible language without translation.

population_and_sample: South African households and municipalities discussed at the macro-policy level (no empirical sample)
exposure: South Africa's Free Basic Water (FBW) policy, Section 9 Water Services Act tariff regulations (rising block tariffs and 6 kilolitre/month free basic allowance), municipal indigent policies, and intergovernmental equitable share transfers
outcome: Household water service access, affordability, coverage, and errors of inclusion and exclusion (discussed using secondary reports only)
rationale: Although the paper directly addresses household water service access (c1) and rule-type tariff, subsidy, and indigent-targeting mechanisms in South Africa (c2), it is a narrative policy overview and practitioner reflection essay by the former Director-General of DWAF rather than an empirical study or systematic empirical synthesis. It has no primary data collection, no empirical analytical method, and no identifiable empirical study design, relying solely on narrative policy history, legal/affidavit excerpts, and descriptive secondary agency figures. Excluded under E05 (No empirical evidence).
